title: One Fact Changes Everything — Treatment vs Control
blurb: The two hierarchies answer different questions. These pairs are where people conflate them.
source: ISO 31000:2018 §6.5 · Hierarchy of controls (NIOSH), applied to AI systems

pairs.dimension: whether the measure changes the hazard or only who pays for it

a.text: The firm adds output validation and human review to a claims model, cutting the rate of wrong denials.
a.why: The probability of the harm actually falls. Reduction is the only treatment that makes the affected person better off.

b.text: The firm buys an insurance policy covering the cost of wrongly denied claims, leaving the model unchanged.
b.why: The claimant is denied at exactly the same rate; only the firm's balance sheet is protected. Insurance is never a control.

pairs.dimension: whether the activity continues at all

a.text: After assessment, the emotion-inference feature is cancelled and removed from the roadmap.
a.why: The activity stops, so the exposure goes to zero. Avoidance is the only treatment with no residual risk to record.

b.text: After assessment, the emotion-inference feature ships with confidence thresholds, subgroup evaluation and human review of low-confidence cases.
b.why: The activity continues at lower likelihood of harm. Substantial mitigation is still reduction, and residual risk still needs an owner.

pairs.dimension: whether the constraint is enforced by the system or by a person

a.text: The deployment pipeline refuses to promote a model whose fairness evaluation has regressed past a threshold.
a.why: The rule executes on every release without anyone choosing to apply it, so deadline pressure cannot erode it.

b.text: The release checklist requires the release manager to confirm that the fairness evaluation has not regressed.
b.why: Identical intent, enforced by human diligence. This is the single most common over-crediting in AI risk assessments.

pairs.dimension: whether the hazardous capability still exists

a.text: The agent's ability to issue refunds is removed from its tool set entirely.
a.why: No capability, no failure mode, and nothing left to monitor. Elimination is the top tier because it retires the whole branch of the risk tree.

b.text: The agent keeps its refund tool, with a hard limit of one refund per session and an amount cap enforced by the tool.
b.why: A strong technical constraint that still leaves a bounded exposure — and leaves the cap itself as something that can be misconfigured.

pairs.dimension: who bears the residual burden of getting it right

a.text: The assistant detects and blocks confidential-looking input before it is sent to the model.
a.why: The system prevents the disclosure regardless of what the user does. The burden sits with the party able to carry it.

b.text: The assistant displays a notice asking users not to paste confidential information.
b.why: The same risk, with the burden moved to the user. Weakest tier, and frequently the only one implemented.

pairs.dimension: whether the risk was knowingly retained at the right authority

a.text: The risk committee records the residual risk, confirms it is within appetite, names an owner and sets a review date.
a.why: Acceptance is an affirmative decision with authority, an owner and a review point. That record is what distinguishes it from neglect.

b.text: The residual risk is known to the delivery team, is not in the risk register, and no one above the team has been told.
b.why: Silence is not acceptance. Without the right authority deciding, there is no treatment at all — only exposure nobody has owned.

pairs.dimension: whether the mechanism or only the setting changed

a.text: A free-generation summariser over clinical notes is replaced with an extractive summariser that can only quote source text.
a.why: The fabrication mechanism is swapped out for one incapable of fabricating, while the purpose survives. Redesign beats tuning.

b.text: The same free-generation summariser is kept, with temperature lowered and a grounding instruction added to the prompt.
b.why: The mechanism that can fabricate is intact and merely discouraged. Useful, and structurally weaker than removing the capability.

pairs.dimension: whether the measure prevents the harm or detects it afterwards

a.text: Retrieval enforces the requesting user's access rights, so unauthorised documents are never returned.
a.why: The harm cannot occur. Prevention is what reduces likelihood; everything else reduces only duration or impact.

b.text: A quarterly audit samples answers and reports any that cited documents the user should not have seen.
b.why: The disclosure already happened, up to three months ago. Detection limits impact and is routinely mistaken for prevention in control catalogues.
